### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d5f76233f435e0ec82110392e1417498ee986fe` — the merge of head `b464a20646d51fddb5751ebc8988cc7ada242b40` into base `72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d5f76233f435e0ec82110392e1417498ee986fe && git checkout 8d5f76233f435e0ec82110392e1417498ee986fe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181 b464a20646d51fddb5751ebc8988cc7ada242b40 && git checkout -B drift-repro 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181 && git merge --no-ff b464a20646d51fddb5751ebc8988cc7ada242b40

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 72b26ed4f5dcdf32b4b167764fa1ecc71121f181` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b464a20646d51fddb5751ebc8988cc7ada242b40`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22853 (body and all six comments: the filing seat's addendum 6109944507, triage 6110285519, the serial note 6110561393, claim 6111650463, os-dev-report 6112597666, the seat's ACCEPT 6112641234, read as a claim to verify), PR #22884 (body, seven-file list, net diff against the merge base 6d5191e69 on `main`), the 38 check-runs on this head, PR #22849 as precedent (body and its two records 6109936970 FAIL and 6110206259 PASS), and the tree at this head for `packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts`, `packages/cli/package.json` with its three entry modules, the lowering's in-tree readers (`lint.ts`, `validate.ts`, `author-time-rules.ts`, `scaffold-validate.ts`, `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/build-shaped-artifact.ts`), every reader of the moved text and `--json` faces under `packages`, `scripts`, `.github`, `examples`, `content/docs` and `docs/qa`, the two changeset gates' readers of the `Clause-②:` line, and #22886's title. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`objectstack build` writes the runtime module from `bodylessCallables` — right, and every stack that got a module before still gets one.** Traced at this head: every `register()` site is paired with either `tryExtractBody` (which adds the ref to `loweredRefs` on success and notes it `refused`, rank 2, on failure) or a `noteUnlowered` call (`functions-entry`, rank 1, at the three `functions` sites; `authored-body`, rank 0, at the hook and action sites). So every registered ref is in `loweredRefs` or in `unlowered`. The old decision was `count - bodyExtracted` above 0 or a warning present. A warning present means a rank-2 row, the highest rank, which `noteUnlowered` never replaces and the filter (`rank above 0 || not lowered`) keeps. `count` above `bodyExtracted` means more refs than extracting slots, so some ref is outside `loweredRefs` and is therefore in `unlowered`, where the filter keeps it. Old true implies new true; the unit pin "the decision only moves from skip to write" asserts exactly that over eight shapes. The four shapes the changeset names now write: the two-level stack and the shared handler (a `functions` entry no longer masked by a callable lowered at two slots), the hook-and-`functions` shape (a rank-1 row kept although its ref is in `loweredRefs`), and a refused slot beside a lowered slot on one function (rank 2 kept). The door file pins the first three writing the module with `pb_score` answering through `loadArtifactBundle`, and both all-body-only CONTROLs still printing the skip line with no `.mjs` in `dist/`; it spawns the CLI, so it sits in the `integration` project and ran in Test Core, green on this head. One further reachable move the enumeration does not name is carried to ②: a hook or action that carries an authored `body` beside an inline handler (rank 0, never lowered) masked by a callable lowered at two or more slots. Old: `count 2, bodyExtracted 2`, no warning, skip. New: its row survives (not in `loweredRefs`), so the module is written. The code is right there too (the single-walk form of that slot already wrote the module on `main`, since `count` exceeded `bodyExtracted` by one).

2. **`--no-runtime-bundle` accept set — a narrowing only; right.** It refuses iff `needsBundle`, so its moved set is exactly item 1's: the four named shapes and the authored-body variant, each pass to refuse; refuse to pass cannot happen (item 1's implication). The message's two numbers moved from `stillNeeded` and `bodyExtractionWarnings.length` to `bodyless.length` and `refusedCallables.length`; its prefix and exit code are unchanged. The only in-repo reader, `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e.test.ts:410`, matches the prefix substring on a single-slot fixture. No doc under `content/docs` or `docs` describes the flag. The changeset states what each number now counts.

3. **`--strict-body` `--json` `issues` — gains rows, strongest-row precedence, list order unchanged; declared; no in-repo consumer reads the old shape.** The old list was `unlowered` minus `loweredRefs`; the new filter keeps every row of that set plus every rank-above-0 row whose ref some slot lowered, so the list is a superset: the gate only moves from pass to refuse. The two new row kinds are a `functions` entry bound to a function some hook or action lowered (PR #22849's "lowered at ANY slot is not a row" pin, replaced by its opposite here) and a refused slot bound to a function another slot lowered. For a ref noted at several unlowered slots the row is now the highest rank's (refusal, then `functions` entry, then authored body) where it was the first noted; a `Map.set` on an existing key keeps its position, so list order is first-noted order, and for every row that already existed (a ref lowered nowhere) first-noted is registration order, as before. The changeset's third BREAKING bullet states both the new rows and the precedence; the PR body names the replaced pin and triage 6110285519 rules the shape the other way. Consumers re-measured at this head: `build-strict-body-count.test.ts:153` and `:167` read origins in list order on fixtures that bind no function at two slots (one refused hook, four, a `functions` entry beside a distinct refused hook), so they are unaffected and are green in Test Core; `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e` reads `error` and `warnings` on this exit; every other `payload.issues` read (`:358`, `:394`, `:460`, `build-multi-package-artifact.e2e:340`) is on another exit; no `--strict-body` invocation in `.github`, `scripts` or `examples`; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:1344` captures the payload and reads no row. The payload's keys are the same five on this exit.

4. **The default warning and its summary count refused handlers once; `--json` `bodyExtractionWarnings` stays per slot — right, and the asymmetry is acceptance-note material.** Both text faces read `refusedCallables` (the list's refusal rows, so each refused handler once); the success payload still publishes `lowering.bodyExtractionWarnings` (`compile.ts:1178`), one record per refusing slot. The door pin reads `1 handler could not be lowered`, one bullet and `1 handler(s) bundled` for a refused hook walked twice. In-repo readers: `hook-body-build-reach.e2e.test.ts:291` matches the phrase without a count and `:306` reads the JSON key's length on a single-slot fixture, both unaffected. `hook-bodies.mdx:348` says a warning is recorded per refusal and carried in `--json`, which still holds. The dev's `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (carrier none) is the right carrier for this: the key keeps its documented meaning and no contract text promises the two faces one number.

5. **`isExtractionRefusal` — package-private; the published surface does not move.** `@objectstack/cli`'s `exports` map is `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` and `./package.json`; `src/index.ts` re-exports command classes only, `src/hook-body.ts` the extractor's two values and two types, `src/console.ts` three console helpers. `lower-callables.ts` is reachable from none, so the new export, like `bodylessCallables` before it, widens nothing a consumer can import through the entry declarations (`files: dist` ships the compiled file, but the `exports` map closes deep subpaths). `UnloweredSlot` and `UNLOWERED_SLOT_RANK` are module-private. `LoweringResult` gains no field. In-tree readers of the lowering: `lint.ts`, `validate.ts`, `author-time-rules.ts` and `scaffold-validate.ts` read `lowered` and `loweredHookRefs`; `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts` calls `extractLoweredBody` itself; `packages/qa/dogfood/test/build-shaped-artifact.ts` reads `count`, `lowered` and `functions`. None reads `bodylessCallables`, so no other command's verdict moves with the population.

6. **`count` and `bodyExtracted` docblocks — right; the computation is untouched.** `count` is still `Object.keys(functions).length` and `bodyExtracted` still increments once per successful extraction; the new text ("registered callables, each once" and "SLOTS that emitted a body") states what the code always computed, which the old wording blurred. `handlersBundled: lowering.count` in the success payload and the skip line's `all N callables` read `count` unchanged.

7. **Test edits — each a faithful re-anchor or a pin that can fail.** `truncation-remainder-notices.test.ts` re-anchors the one capped for-of to ` refusedCallables`; the precedent's remainder line and pointer are pinned byte for byte in the sibling case and are unchanged in the diff. `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` lists `isExtractionRefusal` under NOT_A_GATE, which is right: a type guard over rows `lowerCallables` produced, reading no stack. `lower-callables.test.ts`: five new pins (the `functions` entry beside a lowered hook, a refused slot beside a lowered action with the row being the warning object itself, an authored-body slot taken off by a lowering elsewhere, strongest-row precedence across both walk orders, a two-walk all-clean CONTROL) and the implication pin. The dev's three ablations (the filter, the decision, the warning count) are each reported red and restored; the shapes they name are the ones the pins discriminate.

8. **Docs — right.** `hook-bodies.mdx:174` and `:348` remain true; no page describes `--no-runtime-bundle`; "Flag docs affected by code changes" is green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/22853-runtime-bundle-bodyless.md`: `@objectstack/cli: minor`, conventional `fix(cli)!` summary, a BREAKING section, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, one adr-0087 marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. **Value `no` — right:** no new key on any published payload (the `--json` keys are the same on every exit; the new `issues` rows keep the `{ origin, reason }` and warning shapes that already existed). **Arm `(narrowing)` — right:** ① items 2 and 3 are published CLI verdicts moving pass to refuse. Per AGENTS.md the arm is BREAKING, so the `!`, the banner and the ADR-0087 marker are required and present; `minor` is the launch-window grade. Both Check Changeset runs are green on this head.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — consistent.** No authorable key, published export or stored shape moves and no stored row is read or rewritten, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to derive; the marker closes the other categories on facts. The one-line fix (drop the flag) is a CI-step note, not a metadata prescription.
- **The three carriers — agree on the value, each legal.** The claim 6111650463 and PR body line 2 read bare `Clause-②: no`; the changeset reads `no (narrowing)`. `check-changeset-no-major` reads the PR-body line alone (value `no`, arm none, so the level axis stands down; with `no (narrowing)` it would read `enforce` and find `minor` clean, the same exit), and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm from the changeset (its signal 4) and asks for the breaking kit, which is present. The claim grammar in the dispatch skill is exactly `yes | no`, with a narrowing card declared `no` and owing this review before the queue, and the dev role copies the claim line into the body. So the arm sits on the carrier whose gate enforces it, and the PR body states it in prose one section down. One correction to the seat's ACCEPT: "no gate reads the arm there" is not accurate, since the level-axis gate does read an arm from the PR body; nothing turns on it here because the grade satisfies both readings. PR #22849 carried the arm on its body as well; this PR does not, which is a shape difference and not a false declaration.
- **Every BREAKING sentence holds against the diff, with one enumeration gap.** The first paragraph, the mechanism sentence, the `--strict-body` bullet, the warning-count bullet, the one-line fix and the Unchanged paragraph (whose scope, "each callable bound at one slot and walked once", is exactly the condition under which the old and new decisions coincide) are each right. The `objectstack build` bullet enumerates four moved shapes and the `--no-runtime-bundle` bullet refuses "those stacks"; ① item 1's authored-body variant (an authored `body` beside an inline handler, masked by a callable lowered at two or more slots) is a fifth reachable pass-to-refuse for `--no-runtime-bundle` the enumeration does not name. No sentence is false by it: "Three shapes reached it" names the defect (an entry shipping with no implementation), which that shape does not reach, since the slot runs from its authored body; the one-line fix covers it; and the refusal points at `--strict-body`, whose row names the slot with the reason PR #22849's entry already carries. Remedy, changeset-only and optional for the seat: name the masked callable as "a `functions` entry, or a hook or action carrying an authored `body` beside an inline handler". It does not decide the verdict: the migration AGENTS.md requires is stated, and the precedent FAIL rested on a sentence that was false, which this changeset has none of.
- No `skip-changeset` label; no `packages/spec` path; no governed path in the seven files.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (must the narrowing be declared and reviewed; amend the claim and body to `no (narrowing)`?): answered by the seat as A in substance. Right that the narrowing owes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record before the queue (this is it), right that the changeset is the carrier the breaking gate reads, and the claim grammar backs the bare `no`; the PR-body reading is corrected in ② without effect on the outcome.
- Deviation 1 (minor, BREAKING, `(narrowing)`, marker against the dispatch's `patch` and bare `no`): right; triage's `Clause-②: no` was the claim-grammar shape and the measured narrowing governs the changeset. Deviation 2 (body line bare `no`): ②. Deviation 3 (two source-text pins outside the claim list, `lower-callables.ts` under the claim's conditional): the claim declares both pins by edit, and the conditional was measured met at the base (the hook-and-`functions` shape gave `count 1, bodyExtracted 1` and an empty list), so the producer is the right landing point. Deviation 4 (PR #22849's "lowered at ANY slot" pin replaced by its opposite): right, per triage 6110285519; the precedent PASS record's "does not move" sentence described that head, and this PR moves it deliberately and declares it. Deviation 5 (`--strict-body` machine output moves): declared, ① item 3. Deviations 6 (trailer amended before any push) and 7 (three gates exit 3 then 0 after a rebuild): process notes; the check-runs on the head are the verdicts of record.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (`lowerCallables` re-keys a `functions` entry by its handler's ref, so a key sharing a function or a name with a hook is lost or bound to the wrong code at load): filed by the seat as #22886, open, labelled `finding`, title matching; a class (a) defect with a measured public door, the carrier Prime Directive #10 names. `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (`--json` `bodyExtractionWarnings` per slot beside a text count per callable, carrier none): accepted as an acceptance note, ① item 4.
- Check-runs on `b464a20646d51fddb5751ebc8988cc7ada242b40`, read 2026-10-11T19:29Z: 38 runs, every one `completed`, conclusions `success` or `skipped` only, none failed and none pending. Success: Build Core; Test Core and its six shards; Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards; Dogfood Verify CLI; Temporal Conformance; TypeScript Type Check and its four Type Check runs; Lint & Repo Gates; Check Changeset (both); Governed Surface Queue Guard; the claim, single-writer and part-of guards; Check Documentation Links; Flag docs affected by code changes; Auto Label and Check PR Size (one run each); filter. Skipped: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (both), and the other Auto Label and Check PR Size runs.
